newsitem.title: INDIA: Miss World contest opens, defies protests.
newsitem.headline: Miss World contest opens, defies protests.

text.p: The Miss World beauty contest opened in India with music and the swirl of dancers on Saturday, defying violent protests and threats by militant women to commit suicide by immolation.
The finale of the two-week pageant, with 88 contestants, took place in a fortress-like cricket stadium in Bangalore, where police had clashed with protesters and detained more than 1,000 people.
Hours before the start of the contest, three separate demonstrations led by right-wing Hindu nationalists left clouds of tear gas over roads leading to the outdoor stadium.
Police said about 500 people had been detained.
But they said the leader of a group of women who had threatened to set themselves on fire in the stadium after swallowing cyanide remained at large.
The pageant has been dogged for more than two months by protesters, who claim the beauty show is demeaning to women and undermines India's 5,000-year-old cultural heritage.
The opening 60 minutes of the finale, in light rain, were devoted to traditional Indian dance and music, drawn from the corners of the sprawling country.

Dozens of local dancers dressed in shimmering blue skirts swirled before a large screen depicting images of ancient Hindu temples at the start of the event, which organisers said would be seen by more than two billion television viewers worldwide.
Women in ruby red veils trimmed with gold danced with men wearing turbans and brandishing swords.
Lumbering elephants bedecked with glittering stones later entered the set, based on the ruins of the 14th century Hindu temple complex of Hanpi
Outside, the stadium was surrounded by hundreds of security officers. Spectators were checked for weapons before entering.
Earlier, three separate protests led by right-wing Hindu nationalists left clouds of tear gas over roads to the stadium.
Police said about 500 people were detained during the protests and a similar number had been rounded up earlier in the day to head off trouble.
"We cannot say what the figure (of detained) is. In all it will be over 1,000," a police official said.
Police said three members of parliament from New Delhi and belonging to the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) were among those held in protests with strong political thrusts.
B.S. Yediyurappa, head of the BJP in Karnataka's state assembly, was also held. "I want the resignation of the state government. We are being denied our democratic rights," he said.
Police said up to seven policemen were injured. Casualties among the protesters were unknown.
In one protest, a Reuters reporter saw police with batons and tear gas protesters throwing stones and marching on the Chinnaswamy stadium.
The protests blocked traffic for about two hours in Bangalore, the capital of Karnataka -- Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's home state and India's technology centre.
"It's a police state," shouted Ananth Kumar, a BJP member of parliament, as police bundled him into a van.
"It is a most bizarre situation," Julia Morley, the Miss World organiser, said before the start of the contest.
